No CI edit is needed: `fmt`, `clippy`, `geiger`, and `coverage` sweep members automatically — which also means the crate must be clean under `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` from its first commit. If its entry point is pure I/O with the testable logic in sibling modules, add the `main.rs` to `sonar.coverage.exclusions` (the `servers/ds` shape: `registry.rs` measured, `main.rs` excluded)
- **Errno ABI + generated C headers (slice 5.0):** `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` has two bands (phase-5 decision D7) — the **POSIX block, magnitudes `1..=40`**, at classic book-era MINIX values, which are identical to Linux/musl's (that identity is the whole point: musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and `syscall_ret.c`'s `r > -4096UL` work unmodified), and the **MINIX-specific IPC band at `>= 200`**, taking modern MINIX 3 `sys/sys/errno.h` values (`ENOTREADY` 201, `EDEADSRCDST` 202, `EDONTREPLY` 203, `EGENERIC` 204, `ELOCKED` 208 … plus `EBADSRCDST` 216, the one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT`). Nothing may land in the `41..=199` gap, where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted. Constants are stored **negated**; an `errnos!` macro takes the positive magnitude and emits both the `pub const` and `pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)]` — `ALL` is the single source of truth for the header generator, the `const _` band/distinctness guards, and the host tests, so **add an errno by adding one line to the macro invocation, never by hand-editing a second list**. `tools/gen-c-headers` (package `minixrs-gen-c-headers`, first host/`std` crate in the workspace; lib holds the renderers + tests, `main.rs` is argv/IO only and is Sonar-coverage-excluded via `tools/**/src/main.rs`) prints `include/minixrs/{ipc,com,callnr,errno}.h` from the live constants; **the headers are a build artifact under `target/` and are never committed** (D8 — drift is impossible by construction, and CI asserts nothing was written into the tree). Four things to preserve when extending it: generated C uses **C11 keywords** (`_Static_assert`, `_Alignas` on the struct's *first member* — C11 forbids it on a type declaration — and `_Alignof`), never GNU attributes; `minixrs/ipc.h` **includes nothing** (`offsetof` comes from `__builtin_offsetof` under the private name `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, because Apple's clang redirects `<stddef.h>` to the system header for any `*-musl` triple and would break the hermetic `-nostdlibinc -ffreestanding` CI check); every process gets **both** `<NAME>_PROC_NR` and `<NAME>_EP` (they differ for kernel tasks — `SYSTEM_PROC_NR` is −2, `SYSTEM_EP` is 32766 — and the header `_Static_assert`s the C decode macro against the Rust-computed endpoints); and `minixrs/errno.h` **asserts but never defines** the POSIX block, behind `#ifdef MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, since CI has no musl sysroot and a host `<errno.h>` disagrees (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11) — slice 5.6's `tools/build-musl.sh` must define that macro to make the value check real. `abi-selftest.c` exists because a header is never a translation unit, so without a `.c` file none of the `_Static_assert`s would ever fire. **Adding a request number means editing `tools/gen-c-headers/src/callnr_h.rs` too:** unlike `error.rs`'s `ALL`, the per-band `members` lists in `bands()` are **hand-maintained**, so bumping `NR_*_MSGS` without adding the row leaves the constant silently absent from the generated header — the `c-headers` CI gate still passes, because it compiles a header that simply never mentions it. The crate's own `every_band_member_list_matches_its_count` test is what catches this (it did, in 5.10a), so run `cargo test -p minixrs-gen-c-headers` after any band change, not just `cargo gen-c-headers`
- **Fault-safe user access + the debug channel (slice 5.1):** the kernel **never dereferences a user VA**, not even the active TTBR0's. Every byte in or out of a user address space goes through `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` — `copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, dst)` / `copy_to_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, src)` / `probe_user_range(ttbr0_pa, va, len, write)` — which page-chunks the range, resolves each page with the new `addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>` (the missing member of the `map_page_in`/`unmap_page_in`/`walk_leaves` free-function family; `AddrSpace::walk_pt` delegates to it), and `memcpy`s through the frame's HHDM alias. Consequences to preserve: an unmapped page is a walk miss returning **`EFAULT`, not an EL1 abort** — so **no exception-fixup table is needed or wanted** (D5 rejected the Linux `extable` approach); the copy is **address-space-independent**, so `flush_deliver_msg` can write a receiver's buffer before its TTBR0 is installed (the TTBR0-before-flush ordering in `sched::schedule_next` is no longer load-bearing, only `eret` needs it); `copy_to_user_as` must **check `Prot::writable`**, because the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping that the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes are **all-or-nothing** (probe first) since a 104-byte `Message` is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages. Slice 5.2's grant engine builds on these primitives rather than re-deriving them. `user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate; the page arithmetic (`page_chunks` / `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE`) lives in `kernel-shared/src/message.rs` beside it because the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`. `ipc/message.rs` carries **zero `unsafe`** — messages stage through a `[u8; 104]` — so all raw-pointer work is in `mm::uaccess` alone. Error routing: `EFAULT` to the caller's `x0` via `do_ipc` for the three immediate sites, and to a blocked receiver's **parked `x0`** (`p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64` — the MINIX `retreg` idiom `do_exit::unblock_dependents` uses) for the deferred flush, which also sets/clears the previously-unused `MF_MSGFAILED`. Both traces are **uncounted** (`[efault] proc=… nr=… call=… va=…`, `[efault deliver] proc=… nr=… va=…`) so they are stable boot markers, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form; the `do_ipc` one keys on `result == EFAULT`, which is unambiguous because nothing else in the kernel produces it. **`SYS_DIAGCTL` is the servers' debug channel** (D2) — servers run at EL0 with no console, and this must keep working while grants/TTY/VFS are under construction, so the text rides **inline in the payload** (subcode `0..4`, len `4..8`, up to `DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88` bytes from `DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8`) and needs no user-copy machinery. `kernel/src/system/do_diagctl.rs` prints one line per call as `[diag <name>] <text>`, where `<name>` is the caller's kernel-known `Proc::name` (never payload data, so a server can only identify itself) and text is sanitized to printable ASCII (so one call is always exactly one line — the `grep -aF` marker contract depends on it). `server-rt::diag_print` is the client, chunking longer strings; it is called from **`sef_startup`**, so all six SEF servers emit `[diag <name>] sef ready` at boot. Adding a stub is discouraged: `NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE`, so a fifth stub shifts init's forked children 15 → 16 and breaks checked-in markers — put new probe behavior in an existing stub's prologue (5.1 used stub A's)
- **Grants — the governed cross-address-space copy (slice 5.2, D4):** a granting process keeps its `GrantEntry` table **in its own address space** and registers `(addr, entries)` with `SYS_SETGRANT`; `SYS_SAFECOPY` reads the entry back out of the *granter's* address space on every call, so a granter revokes by writing its own memory and the kernel caches nothing that could go stale. The ABI is `kernel-shared/src/grant.rs` — flat `#[repr(C)]` `GrantEntry` (flags/seq/who_to/who_from/addr/len, 32 bytes, layout pinned by `offset_of!` asserts because the kernel decodes it from raw bytes), MINIX's CPF flag values, and `GRANT_SHIFT = 20` id packing (`grant_id`/`grant_idx`/`grant_seq`). The engine is one new function beside the 5.1 trio, `mm::uaccess::copy_between_as(src_ttbr0, src_va, dst_ttbr0, dst_va, len)`: probe both ranges, then walk-and-`memcpy` per `dual_page_chunks` — **all-or-nothing on the destination**, and its `Prot::writable` check is load-bearing (a granter may *lie* about writability, and the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 bits do not police). `verify_grant` (`system/do_safecopy.rs`) checks, in MINIX's order: `okendpt` the granter, table registered + idx in range, entry reads back (a walk miss is hidden as **`EPERM`, not `EFAULT`**, so a grantee cannot probe the granter's address space), `CPF_USED|CPF_VALID`, `seq` matches the id, requested access ⊆ flags, `who_to` == caller's *stored endpoint*, `offset + bytes <= len`. `CPF_DIRECT` resolves the memory to the granter; `CPF_MAGIC` resolves it to `who_from` and additionally requires the granter's `Priv::flags & SYS_PROC` (minix.rs's stand-in for MINIX's hardcoded VFS/MIB list); `CPF_INDIRECT` is a documented `EINVAL`. `SYS_COPY` is the same engine with no grant — `resolve_target` on both endpoints (`SELF` works), `k_call_mask` is the only gate, the `do_vmctl` trust stance. All three are routed from the **target-taking `match`** in `kernel_call_dispatch`, `SYS_SETGRANT` included: it is caller-local in effect but needs `&mut Priv`, which `dispatch_caller_local` cannot hand out. It also **rejects a shared priv slot** (`proc_nr != Some(caller)` → `EPERM`) — one table address cannot describe several processes' memory — and **both `do_exit` and `do_exec`** clear a dedicated slot's registration: exit so a recycled slot cannot inherit a stale table address, exec because the registered VA describes the image being discarded while the privilege slot survives. Client side: `server-rt::GrantPool<const N>` is a **value the server owns** (a `main`-frame local, never `init_fresh`'s frame), which is what keeps `server-rt` `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; `ensure_registered` compares the pool's live address against the last registered one and re-issues `SYS_SETGRANT` if they differ. Byte buffers use the new `kernel-shared::message::user_range_ok` (no alignment requirement, unlike `user_va_ok`, which stays right for the 8-aligned grant table). Traces are head-carved (6) like `do_vmctl`'s — these are low-rate callers the `[ksys N]` sampler never catches. A server that holds `SYS_COPY`/`SYS_SAFECOPY` and serves clients that do not must take the **granter from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, never from the payload** — a caller-supplied granter endpoint turns that server into a confused deputy, aiming a privileged cross-AS copy wherever the caller points. Same anti-spoof rule `DS_PUBLISH` already relies on; apply it to every grant-id-carrying request (CDEV since 5.3, BDEV/FS bands to come). The live demo is VFS → PM (`PM_GRANT_TEST`, demo-only, retire it when CDEV lands): a direct grant, the same bytes again via `SYS_COPY` for a checksum comparison, a magic read out of init's text page, and **seven denial probes** (`[diag pm] grant.deny ok n=7`) that keep every validator exercised by a boot marker
- **The console: user-space TTY, device memory, and the CDEV band (slice 5.3, D1):** the first user-space *driver* — `drivers/tty` (workspace member, packed at **index 2** of `kernel/build.rs`'s `servers` array, between `ds` and `vfs`, so the console is in its receive loop before its first client) owns the PL011 and serves `CDEV_WRITE`. **Device memory comes from reading `MAIR_EL1`, never writing it:** writing byte *i* retroactively retypes every live mapping using `AttrIndx=i`, including Limine's TTBR1 kernel/HHDM mappings whose indices this repo cannot enumerate. `mmu::init_device_attr_idx` (called once from `userland_bootstrap`, before any device mapping) scans bytes **1..8** for `0x04` (Device-nGnRE, preferred) else `0x00` (nGnRnE) — sufficient because an *unprogrammed* MAIR byte reads `0x00`, which is itself a valid MMIO encoding, so "already Device" and "unused" coincide; only those two qualify (nGRE would gather two `DR` stores into one lost character, GRE would let the `DR` store pass the `FR` poll). On QEMU today it picks index 1; `[mair] device attr_idx=… byte=…` is **forensic, not a boot marker** (firmware-dependent). `Prot` grew a third field, `device` (+ `Prot::DEVICE_RW`), which is a compile error at every struct literal — the point; `do_vmctl`'s `pt_map` answers `device: false` **permanently**, because D1 rejected a VM-mediated `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS` for Phase 5 (revisit for Phase-6 virtio-mmio, gated on a per-driver PA whitelist). `pte_prot` decodes `device` **statelessly** (`pte_attr_idx_of(pte) != ATTR_IDX_NORMAL`), sound because the kernel emits only two indices and byte 0 is pinned Normal-WB (`const _: () = assert!(ATTR_IDX_NORMAL == 0)`). The **total invariant** is `map_page_in`'s pair of asserts against the extracted `mm::is_usable_pa`: `prot.device ⇒ ¬RAM` and `¬prot.device ⇒ RAM`, so every leaf is provably `(RAM ∧ ¬device)` or `(device ∧ ¬RAM)` — the lemma that makes `if !prot.device { free_frame(…) }` sound in **five** leaf sweeps (`do_exit::teardown_addrspace`, `do_fork::copy_addrspace`'s copy loop *and* its OOM unwind, `do_vmctl::pt_unmap`, `userland::destroy_addrspace_with_leaves`); `free_frame` keeps its loud out-of-range assert deliberately (a silent skip would demote a forged-PA/double-free into an untraceable leak). Fork **re-maps** a device leaf rather than copying it (MMIO is shared, and a `memcpy` through the cacheable HHDM alias would read side-effecting registers into RAM), and `mm::uaccess::resolve_copyable` rejects a device leaf as copy source *or* destination (`EFAULT`). `teardown_addrspace` is now `pub(crate)` (and `system::do_exit` a `pub(crate) mod`) returning `(freed, devs)` — hence `devs=` on `[ksys SYS_EXIT]` — for `userland::device_teardown_selftest`, which is **load-bearing, not decoration**: TTY never exits, so the device arm would be dead code on a live landmine whose failure is a *kernel panic*; it runs unconditionally at boot (so `--no-default-features` covers it) and asserts **both** counts, `[devmap] selftest ok freed=0 devs=1` (a guard skipping every leaf gives `devs=0`). The device VA map is a new module, `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs` — an *address* ABI, not a message one: `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE = 0x4000_0000` (one whole L1 slot), `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE = 16 MiB`, `TTY_UART_VA` = page 0; **not** emitted in the generated C headers. A `const _` on the region *bases* is *not enough* — it proves only where each starts, and two grow on request (the mmap bump cursor, and the heap's end via `set_brk`), so **both** carry a runtime `region::REGION_LIMIT` check (`ENOMEM` past it). The pre-map lives in `load_boot_server` gated on `nr == TTY_PROC_NR`, **deliberately not in `load_exec_image`** (shared with `do_exec`, so every exec'd binary would inherit a device window — and conversely a proc that exec'd would *lose* its window, which is why `do_exec` drops the device count); **no TLB maintenance**, because the AS was built moments ago and never installed in TTBR0 (a recycled ASID is clean — `teardown_addrspace` flushes before `free_asid`) and `switch_ttbr0_with_asid` already issues `isb; tlbi aside1; dsb ish; isb` on TTY's first schedule — same reasoning `SERVER_STACK_VA` already relies on, do not diverge. **CDEV band** `CDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xB00` (between PM `0x700` and VM `0xC00`; VFS took `0x800` in 5.4 and BDEV `0xA00` in 5.7, leaving `0x900` reserved for the VFS↔FS band in 5.8, and `callnr_h.rs`'s `bands_are_in_ascending_numeric_order` enforces where each goes — slices 5.3–5.6 recorded the BDEV/FS pairing the other way round in four comments, corrected in 5.7; only the ascending order is load-bearing): `CDEV_WRITE {minor 0..4, grant_id 4..8, len 8..12, offset 16..24}` — **no payload `granter`** (the driver takes it from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the 5.2 confused-deputy rule); reply `m_type` **is the byte count** (`>= 0`, `0` legal), and a request longer than `CDEV_MAX_IO = 256` is a **short write, not a failure** (POSIX `write()`, and what lets a driver stage through a `main`-frame buffer with no allocator; the client re-sends with `offset` advanced). `CDEV_READ` was absent until slice 5.11 defined it (reading `/dev/zero` needs it; TTY serves it in Phase 6, when RX gets `SYS_IRQCTL`). A driver **replies** to an unknown `m_type` where DS may drop one — a driver's clients all SENDREC, and a dropped request blocks the caller forever; and a negative `SYS_SAFECOPY` result is relayed **verbatim** (`EPERM` = bad grant vs `EFAULT` = unmapped buffer are different client bugs). PL011 register offsets are **duplicated** in `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/uart.rs` and `drivers/tty/src/pl011.rs` and cannot be shared (the kernel crate is bare-metal-only and pinned by `forced-target`, so never a user-space dep; a register layout is a hardware fact, not a shared ABI); `drivers/tty` deliberately does **not** depend on `minixrs-driver-rt` (a 4-line placeholder — Phase 6 makes that move plus the `kernel/build.rs` watch entry). Helpers lifted into `server-rt` this slice: `payload.rs` (`rd_i32`/`wr_i32`/`rd_u64`/`wr_u64`/`buf_addr`, measured, replacing PM/DS/VM/SCHED copies — uses `checked_add` because servers ship `--release` with `overflow-checks = false`, where `off + 4` *wraps* and is safe only by accident while panicking under `cargo test`), `kcall.rs` (`sys_safecopy`/`sys_copy` out of PM, coverage-excluded), `diag_fmt` (PM's `diag_line` promoted), `sef_retrieve_from_ds`. **DS publish-before-retrieve is not deterministic** — it works only because `build.rs` packs TTY before VFS — so a DS lookup must **fall back to `boot_endpoint(…)`** and emit a distinguishable diag line, keeping the rest of the proof alive while the `cdev.ds ok` marker (and only it) disappears. **TCG caveat:** the Device *attribute* is not observably load-bearing under QEMU — its PL011 works through Normal-WB (which is what the kernel's own HHDM alias has always been), so substituting `ATTR_IDX_NORMAL` changes no marker; the attribute is proved by construction and assertion, as are the `FR.TXFF` poll (TCG's FIFO never fills) and LF→CRLF (`grep -aF` cannot express `\r`)

- **The POSIX write path — VFS, magic grants, and the fd table (slice 5.4):** `VFS_RQ_BASE = 0x800` (between PM `0x700` and CDEV `0xB00`), one request: `VFS_WRITE {fd 0..4, len 4..8, buf 8..16}` — a **raw buffer address, not a grant id**, because VFS's client is an ordinary user process with no grant table. Reply `m_type` **is the byte count** (`>= 0`), the `CDEV_WRITE` contract and what musl's `write()` returns. VFS is the granter: `do_write` issues a **`CPF_MAGIC` grant naming the caller's buffer with the driver as grantee**, so the bytes move in **one** copy, caller → driver, and VFS never touches them (first magic-grant consumer on a real data path). **The grant's owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`, never a payload field** — VFS holds `SYS_PROC`, so a caller-supplied owner would let any client aim a privileged cross-AS copy at a third party; this is the 5.2/5.3 confused-deputy rule applied to the *granting* side, and there must never be a field for it. **VFS absorbs short writes** (`CDEV_MAX_IO` is a driver staging detail that must not reach `write()`'s return): `write_all` re-sends with `offset` advanced over the *same* grant until the buffer is out, clamps `off` with `.min(len)` so an over-reporting driver cannot walk past the buffer, breaks on `n == 0` rather than spinning, and on an error **after partial progress reports the progress** (POSIX: those bytes really went out). VFS **replies to an unknown `m_type`** (`ENOSYS`) — TTY's rule; its clients all SENDREC. `servers/vfs/src/fd.rs` is the fd table: `NR_FDS = 4` (VFS-local, *not* ABI; the 4th slot makes "past the end" and "not open" distinguishable), rows sized from `com::NR_SERVED_PROCS` with the usual `const _` guard, fds 0/1/2 pre-opened to `CDEV_MINOR_CONSOLE` in every row. Storage is an **immutable `static` until slice 5.8's `open`** — nothing mutates, so VFS keeps zero `unsafe`; `resolve_in` takes the rows as a borrowed slice precisely so it survives the switch to the `UnsafeCell<[FdRow; N]>` newtype (`vm/region.rs` shape) untouched. `user_range_ok` in `do_write` is **defence in depth, not the gate** — removing it moves no marker, because the kernel's page-table walk answers `EFAULT` regardless (D5). `populate_user_priv`'s `USER_IPC_TO = [PM, VFS]` widens the shared USER slot to `ipc_to = {PM, VFS}`; every entry costs a **pair** of bits, since `init_boot_image` fills a boot server's bitmap only over `[0, n_active)` and `USER_PRIV_ID` is 20, so each **reverse reply edge must be opened explicitly** (drop the forward bit → init's SENDREC is refused and every marker vanishes; drop the reverse → the write still *happens* and only the reply is refused, so init hangs mid-SENDREC and takes the fork/exec/exit cycle markers with it). init is the client and reports **through the path under test** (it has no `SYS_DIAGCTL` — user grade), which is why a successful write's count needs its own marker: `vfs.long ok match=1` alongside the `vfs-loop-end` tail, because a `write()` that moves every byte and replies `OK` prints the tail and is still broken. Pure logic lives in `servers/vfs/src/write.rs` (`parse`/`validate`/`advance`), the `drivers/tty/src/cdev.rs` split — not just tidiness: **a retry loop's rules for a misbehaving peer are unreachable while the peer works** (a driver reporting `0`, or more than it was asked for), so lifting the loop body into a step function is the only way to test them; it also keeps them Sonar-measured, since `main.rs` is coverage-excluded and a sibling module is not. The generated C header emits `VFS_WRITE` but **not** its payload offsets — deferred to slice 5.6's `write()` wrapper, which is exactly the C that will need them

- **The exec initial stack — SysV frame, auxv, and a marker that proved nothing (slice 5.5, D13):** `SYS_EXEC` no longer just points `sp_el0` at the stack page top — it builds the **Linux/SysV initial frame** there first (`[argc][argv…][NULL][envp…][NULL][auxv pairs][AT_NULL]` then the NUL-terminated name, padded so `sp` is 16-aligned; `argc = 1`, empty envp) so musl's crt/`__libc_start_main`/`__init_tls` run **unpatched** — the standing keep-the-musl-diff-minimal principle only holds if the *kernel* supplies the frame. The byte layout lives in `kernel-shared/src/execstack.rs` (`build_initial_stack`, pure, zero `unsafe`, host-tested — the `user_va_ok`/`page_chunks` carve-out, since the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`); `do_exec` stages it in a `[u8; INITIAL_STACK_MAX]` **kernel-stack** buffer and installs it with 5.1's `copy_to_user_as`, which is address-space-independent by design, so no new copy machinery and the TTBR0 need not be installed. Both frame failures (`None` → `E2BIG`, copy error → `ENOMEM`) run `do_exit::teardown_addrspace` on the **fresh** image and return **before** the point of no return, extending `load_exec_image`'s leave-the-target-on-its-old-image invariant rather than weakening it. `elf::load_into` now returns a `LoadedElf { entry, phdr_va: Option<u64>, phnum, phentsize }`, `phdr_va` computed in the existing segment loop from the first `PT_LOAD` whose *file* range covers `[e_phoff, e_phoff + phnum*phentsize)`; `ExecImage` carries the three through. Auxv order is **fixed by the caller** (`AT_PHDR`, `AT_PHNUM`, `AT_PHENT`, `AT_PAGESZ`), not Linux's incidental order, so the trace and tests are deterministic. The `AT_*` values are the Linux/SysV ones and are deliberately **not** emitted by `gen-c-headers` — musl defines them itself. **`AT_PHDR` needs a linker-script opt-in, and the plan's "when the first PT_LOAD covers the ELF header" was otherwise *never* true:** lld's default aarch64 `max-page-size` (64 KiB) puts PT_LOAD #0 at file offset `0x10000`, leaving `e_phoff = 64` in an unmapped prefix, so a reported VA would fault `__init_tls`. `userland/worker/user.ld` therefore takes the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom (`text PT_LOAD FILEHDR PHDRS FLAGS(5)` + `. = <base> + SIZEOF_HEADERS`), giving PT_LOAD #0 at offset `0x0` / vaddr `0x100000` — both still page-aligned, so the loader's strict checks are untouched; only the entry moves one page up. **Server `user.ld`s stay unchanged** (boot-loaded images keep `sp = SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE` and never read an auxv). Any new exec'able binary that wants `AT_PHDR` must copy that idiom and be re-checked with `llvm-readobj --program-headers`. **EL0 is where the frame is proved:** `[exec] argc=1 envc=0 auxv=4 sp=0x` only says the kernel *thinks* it wrote one, so `worker` reads its real `sp` and validates the frame (alignment, argc, the `argv[0]` bytes through the stored pointer, both NULLs, `AT_PAGESZ`, and a phdr that reads back as `PT_LOAD` at the link base), returning `0` or the **1-based number of the first failing check**. That is what its `_start` is `#[unsafe(naked)]` + `naked_asm!("mov x0, sp", "b {main}")` for — a prologue could perturb `sp`, and taking the value in `x0` from the kernel would prove nothing about `SP_EL0`; the `#[cfg(all(not(test), target_arch = "aarch64"))]` split with a plain `main(0)` fallback is `minixrs-ipc`'s exact pattern, needed because CI's blocking clippy runs on x86_64 (the fallback must still *call* `main`, or it is dead code under `-D warnings`). The verdict rides out as the **exit status**, not a console line — worker runs once per init fork cycle — with a direct `stack FAIL` write to fd 2 as backup for the case where the status path is what broke. **The trap worth remembering: PM's `mproc::seed` parents the demo stubs to init, and stub D is SIGSEGV'd on purpose early in boot, so init's *first* `wait()` reaps that zombie (status 0), not a child it forked.** A marker keyed on "the first reap" printed `exec stack ok` beside 81 `worker: stack FAIL` lines under the argc mutation — vacuous, and *only* under default features, since `--no-default-features` has no stubs and its first reap really is the forked child. Key any reap-derived marker on the child's **pid** (`alloc_pid` never returns 0, so 0 is the "not yet" sentinel), and treat "a marker can be right in one feature config and prove nothing in the other" as the general lesson: mutation-test in the config that has the stubs. **The same trap has a second mouth:** `mproc::handle_kill_in` zombifies a *signalled* process without touching `exit_status`, so a probe that died before reporting is reaped with status 0 — and `validate` dereferences pointers out of the frame, so a bad enough frame faults it into VM's SIGSEGV arm, which prints no `!!! EL0 data abort` for the forbidden list to catch. Hence the pass is the positive sentinel `execstack::EXEC_STACK_PROBE_PASS` (`0x5A`) and status 0 prints `FAIL no-verdict`. General rule for any probe reporting through an exit status: **encode the pass, never the absence of a failure**

- **C on minix.rs — the musl port, the sysroot, and the ABI freeze (slice 5.6, milestone A):** the libc is a **git submodule at `external/musl`** → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking branch **`minixrs`** (the port; `main` is a pristine upstream mirror with nothing on it), based on tag **`v1.2.6`**. The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` is archived and nothing was carried over. The fork's whole delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` + `src/minixrs/` + a brand block in `crt/crt1.c` + `MINIXRS.md`, and staying that small is the design goal — **musl globs `src/*/`, so `src/minixrs/` needs no Makefile edit**. Every `__syscallN` calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the *Linux* number musl still emits and issues a server round-trip (`writev`/`write` → `VFS_WRITE`, `exit`/`exit_group` → `PM_EXIT`, `set_tid_address` → 1, `ioctl` → `-ENOTTY`, everything else `-ENOSYS`); musl's ~297 call sites stay untouched, which is what lets ~1900 files rebase for free. `syscall_ret.c` is untouched because D7's magnitudes (`1..=40`, `>=200`) all sit inside its `> -4096UL` window. **`ioctl` → `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing**: it makes `__stdout_write` set `f->lbf = -1`, so stdout is **fully buffered** and `printf` only reaches the console via `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit` — the milestone marker therefore proves the flush path too. Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts that must be **re-verified, never assumed, on any musl bump** (all re-read against v1.2.6, recorded in the fork's `MINIXRS.md`): `__init_libc` early-returns past its `ppoll` when `AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` are absent (they read 0); `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the canary arithmetically; `__init_tp`'s only syscall is `set_tid_address` (`__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm since v1.2.6) and it **walks `libc.auxv`**, so the auxv must stay `AT_NULL`-terminated; `__init_tls` uses static `builtin_tls` absent a `PT_TLS` (so no `mmap`) and walks 5.5's `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT`. **`tools/build-musl.sh`** builds an out-of-tree sysroot into `target/musl-sysroot` (the submodule work tree stays **pristine** — the `c-headers` job asserts a clean `git status`), keyed by a `.stamp` of submodule SHA + toolchain; `RANLIB` is **`llvm-ar s`**, because the pinned toolchain ships `llvm-ar` but **not** `llvm-ranlib`. It also runs the **real D7 errno *value* check** 5.0 deferred here — the opt-in POSIX block compiled against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` under `-nostdinc -isystem <sysroot>/include`; the CI `c-headers` job keeps only the hermetic stand-in check. `userland/hello` is **not a cargo crate** — `hello.c` + `hello.ld` compiled by clang and linked by `rust-lld` inside `kernel/build.rs` (`build_hello` at the time, `build_hello_musl` since P3c added the SDK flavor beside it; *in the musl flavor* — the SDK flavor uses neither `hello.ld` nor `rust-lld`), packed under proc_nr `-1` like `worker`. **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT (`.stamp`), not the submodule** (both sysroots, since P3c), and packs the `worker` ELF *under the name* `hello` with a `cargo::warning` — checking the submodule would let a fresh clone trigger a multi-minute libc build from inside a build script. That substitution is why `worker`'s `ARGV0_NAMES` is the **set** `{worker, hello}` rather than one literal: it checks the exact `argv[0]` bytes the kernel wrote, so the hardcoded `b"worker"` made a *missing sysroot* print `worker: stack FAIL` — a **forbidden** marker — making an absent optional dependency indistinguishable from a broken exec ABI. **Boot the fallback config when you change it**; two readings of the name-level substitution missed this and only running it caught it. musl's `vfprintf` needs soft-float **binary128** builtins (`__multf3`/`__floatsitf`/…; aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad) which musl's configure finds no library for: they come from **`compiler_builtins` as built by `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`** — the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does **not** export the C-ABI names, so glob the nested target dir, never the sysroot. `hello.ld` is `worker/user.ld` plus what only a musl link brings — `.init`/`.fini` (they define the `_init`/`_fini` `crt1.c` passes to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`, `.data.rel.ro` — because **an orphan section past the last `PT_LOAD` is a silent load failure**; the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom is mandatory (not just an auxv nicety as for Rust: `__init_tls` dereferences `AT_PHDR`). No `PT_TLS` — musl keeps `errno` in the pthread struct via `tpidr_el0`, so `libc.a` has no `.tdata`/`.tbss`. **The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB worst chain) and was NOT grown** — but v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` allocates a **VLA** (~512 B for `%f`, **~7.4 KB for `%Lf`**), so a future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it and *no static frame scan will predict that*. `PM_EXEC` gained a name payload (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`, reusing `EXEC_NAME_LEN`), PM's `EXEC_TARGET` is gone, and **init alternates `worker`/`hello`** (`EXEC_TARGETS`, worker **first** — `probe_pid` keys 5.5's verdict on the first child) so the exec-stack proof survives the C milestone; the target is chosen *before* the fork so both halves of the SENDREC agree. The boot marker is **`name=hello entry=` with no `target=` slot**: init's fork pool gives `hello` slot 15 stub-free but **16** with stubs, so a slot-keyed marker passes in one config and is vacuous in the other. **ABI freeze (D8): past this slice `Message` layout, call numbers, endpoints, and errnos change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos** — there is now C in another repository depending on all four. Since the port branch is **force-pushed** on rebase, a fork rebase and the `external/musl` bump must land in the **same PR**, or this repo pins an orphaned commit

- **Block storage — the BDEV band, the `memory` ramdisk, and a compile-time filesystem (slice 5.7, D3):** a MinixFS v3 image is built **at compile time** by `tools/mkfs-mfs` (a `[lib] + [[bin]]` host crate whose **library `kernel/build.rs` calls directly as a `[build-dependencies]` path dep** — the `brand::scan_brand` precedent, no nested host cargo; cargo re-runs a build script when a build-*dependency* changes, so neither it nor `fs/mfs` needs a `rerun-if-changed` entry), packed into the MXBI archive as a **non-ELF blob** under `com::ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME = "rootfs"` / `EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`, copied into RAM frames at boot, and mapped `Prot::RW_DATA` into the `memory` driver's address space. **`BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`** (D13; `0x900` stays reserved for 5.8's FS band — four in-tree comments said the reverse and were corrected here, since only *ascending order* is load-bearing). Payload mirrors CDEV — `{minor, grant, len, block}` — with **no granter field** (`m_source`, the confused-deputy rule) and **no grant-offset field** (every client through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0). Reply `m_type` **is the byte count**. Two deliberate departures from CDEV, each with its own doc comment: **an over-long or out-of-range request is `EINVAL`, not a short read** (a short *write* is a POSIX contract clients loop over; a short *block read* is useless — a filesystem cannot interpret half a block — and `EIO` stays reserved for Phase 6's real media errors, where the request was well-formed and the *device* failed); and **`BDEV_WRITE` was defined by this slice and answered `EROFS`** (it stores for real as of 5.10a — see that bullet), not `ENOSYS`, because `ENOSYS` is already the unknown-`m_type` answer and reusing it would make "doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses" indistinguishable — which is what let 5.10a change one line inside one arm. **Kernel side:** `uspace::RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE = 0x8000_0000` (one L1 slot, 4 MiB, `RAMDISK_VA` = page 0) is placed **above** the device window on purpose — `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the *lowest* kernel-owned window, so VM needs **no edit** when a window is added, and `assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE)` is what keeps that true (it also makes the ramdisk's separation from every *process* VA transitive, which is why `userland.rs`'s VA-collision block needs no new entries — say so, or someone adds six redundant asserts). The pre-map is a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` arm in `load_boot_server` beside TTY's, **not** in `load_exec_image` (shared with `do_exec`); no TLB maintenance (TTY's two reasons), no cache maintenance (kernel writes and MEM reads the same PA through Normal-WB mappings, and it is data, so no icache concern), and **not** the TTY device-page problem — RAM mapped non-device takes the ordinary `free_frame` path in all five leaf sweeps. Every step `.expect()`s: a `let _ = map_page_in(..)` would turn a non-advancing loop into a 1-page ramdisk with 255 leaked frames instead of an `AlreadyMapped` panic. New selector **`GET_RAMDISK = 64`** returns `(va, len)` and is **gated on `caller.nr == MEM_PROC_NR` → `EPERM`** (the VA is meaningless in any other AS); no new kernel call and no new kernel statics — the VA is a const and the length is `module_by_name("rootfs")`'s. `pack_mxbi` gained `u32` asserts on offset/length (unchecked casts, the latent class `checked_add` exists to kill). **The driver contains no `unsafe` block and never dereferences the mapping**: client transfers are `sys_safecopy`, and the boot self-check is `sys_copy(SELF, …, SELF, …)`, so a page that failed to map is an `EFAULT` *return value* rather than an EL0 abort — hence no MMIO sibling module and no new Sonar exclusion. `server-rt::sys_getinfo` is new, with `sef_startup`'s inline `GET_WHOAMI` refactored onto it so every server's `sef ready` marker proves the refactor. **Three scope amendments forced by repo lessons, all load-bearing:** (a) the image is a **fixed** `ROOTFS_IMAGE_BLOCKS = 256` (1 MiB), because the musl-sysroot-absent fallback packs the 15 KB `worker` ELF as `hello` and a content-sized image would make every size-derived marker config-dependent — the 5.5/5.6 trap; oversizing is a build failure naming one constant; (b) **`/etc/pattern`, 40 KiB, is mandatory**, because `hello` is ~200 KB = 49 blocks and forces the single-indirect arm but the *fallback* `hello` is 4 blocks — inside the 7 direct zones — so both that arm and mkfs's indirect writer would be dead in exactly the config CI's non-QEMU jobs build; (c) **MEM's init check is device-level, not format-level** — a block driver must not depend on the filesystem format (Phase 6 unwinds that when virtio-blk replaces MEM under an unchanged MFS), so mkfs writes a 32-byte **image header** into block 0's unused boot block (bytes `0..1024`, which MFS never reads) plus a 32-byte **tail label** in a reserved last zone, MEM verifies those, and format-level facts are verified by a *client through a real BDEV round trip*. That header ABI lives in **`kernel-shared::rootfs`** (mkfs writes it, MEM and VFS read it, none may depend on the others — the `ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME` reason); `image.rs` re-exports it. The **tail label is not decoration**: a copy loop that failed to advance maps 256 pages of block 0 and passes every header check — mutation-tested, and the only marker that moved was `ramdisk FAIL tail label`. `fs/mfs` gains the pure read path (`superblock`/`inode`/`dirent`/`layout`/`read`, `no_std`, `forbid(unsafe_code)`, **one dependency**) and is **I/O-free by construction** — every reader takes bytes the caller already fetched, which is both what makes it host-testable with no fake device and the shape 5.8's server needs; `zone_for_offset` distinguishes a `Hole` (reads as zeroes) from `OutOfRange` (past the single-indirect span — explicit, never silent zeroes), and double-indirect is justified out arithmetically: `7 + 1024` zones is 4.03 MiB, which is also why the VA window is 4 MiB. VFS's demo runs **last** in `main`'s prologue (a hang localizes to `bdev.*` instead of blacking out 5.2/5.3/5.4's markers — do not tidy the prologue into alphabetical order) and exists because **there is no successful `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere else in the tree**: `BDEV_READ` is the first copy that writes into a grantee's buffer and succeeds, so without it the kernel's `CPF_WRITE` + `Prot::writable` success path stays unproven until 5.8. Its granted buffer is a 32-byte **local**, not a `.rodata` static (the driver writes into it) and not a whole block — **do not grow VFS's one-page stack for a demo that dies in 5.8**, and note that a 4096-byte local would fault into VM's SIGSEGV arm, which prints no `!!! EL0 data abort` for the forbidden list to catch. `module_by_name` is now a namespace shared by ELFs and blobs: asking `do_exec` for `"rootfs"` fails safely (`scan_brand` rejects), but **5.9's path→module resolution must not be able to name it**

- **The SDK toolchain flavor — `kernel/build.rs` consumes `$MINIXRS_SDK` (P3c, toolchain milestone M3a):** slice 5.6 ran C on minix.rs through a *stand-in* triple (`--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, a hand-written `hello.ld`, a globbed `compiler_builtins` rlib, a hand-assembled `rust-lld` line); M3's claim is that all of it collapses into `clang --target=aarch64-unknown-minixrs hello.c -o hello`, and it does — the patched driver supplies `-static`, `--image-base=0x100000` (LLVM patch 0006, which is *why* this flavor needs no linker script), both `-z` flags (D13), the crt objects + `-lc` from the sysroot, and `libclang_rt.builtins.a` for the quad-float helpers. **The port was never the remaining work; the toolchain flavor was.** Selection is **three-way** — `HelloFlavor::{Sdk, Musl, Worker}` — and `Musl` is **not a fallback but `qemu-smoke`'s real dependency** (no CI job installs an SDK, and `tests/qemu-boot.expected` requires the five C markers); only `Worker` loses markers. **Once an SDK is usable every failure is a `panic!`, never a demotion**, because the boot markers are **byte-identical across flavors** — the log physically cannot distinguish them, so a silent demotion turns "your patched clang regressed" into "nothing looks wrong"; the panic carries prefix + stamp + a `clang -###` reproduce line + the `MINIXRS_SDK=/nonexistent` escape hatch. `usable_sdk` probes **exactly three files** (`bin/clang`, `sysroot/.stamp`, `sysroot/usr/lib/libc.a`) and deliberately **not** the crt objects, builtins archive, or `lib/clang/<ver>` resource dir — the driver names those and **nothing here may hard-code the `22`**; a sysroot missing them is a *broken* SDK, which must fail loudly. Both stamps are watched with `rerun-if-changed` **unconditionally**: watching the SDK's only when it exists looks like a free optimization but breaks "run the sysroot builder, then `cargo kernel-aarch64`" — a *declared-but-missing* path is exactly what makes cargo notice the stamp **appearing**. `clang_command` scrubs `CPATH`/`*_INCLUDE_PATH`/`LIBRARY_PATH`/`SDKROOT` from **every** clang site (the `.S` loop included, a no-op there today): clang folds those into the **front** of the include search list, ahead of the sysroot, and **`-nostdinc` does not suppress them** — verified, a host `C_INCLUDE_PATH` really did sort first — so a foreign `errno.h` would shadow musl's and D7 turns on those values. (`/usr/local/include` survives the scrub because the *fork's driver* injects it; it sorts after the sysroot, so it can only add headers musl lacks — do not "fix" it with `-nostdlibinc`, which would drop the sysroot too.) **No pack-time ELF/loader gate, and that is now measured rather than argued:** an image-base regression is already loud — mutation-testing `-Wl,--image-base=0x200000` cost `name=hello entry=` *and* all five C markers, because `load_exec_image`'s `SERVER_STACK_VA` map returns `AlreadyMapped` and the exec unwinds; a gate would mean duplicating a private kernel const to re-detect what the kernel already refuses. Loader rules stay tooling's `verify/check-image.sh`, by hand. Measured: SDK **46,664 B / 4 `PT_LOAD`s** vs musl **200,152 B / 3**, both entry `0x101000`, both a megabyte clear of `SERVER_STACK_VA` — and 46,664 B is **12 MFS blocks**, still past the 7 direct zones, so slice 5.7's `/etc/pattern` mandate is unchanged. **Never write inside `$MINIXRS_SDK`** (tooling's `build-musl.sh` does `rm -rf $SDK/sysroot`); all output goes to `target/hello/`, which **both flavors share**, so read it only after a *successful* build of the flavor you mean. Two things nothing enforces, both manual: the SDK links **its own** musl (the stamp's `musl=<sha>` is a merge commit of `external/musl`'s HEAD, so an equality check is impossible — rebase the fork without re-running tooling's `build-sysroot.sh` and the two flavors silently test different libc code), and the stamp's `minixrs=<sha>` is a **snapshot** of the installed `minixrs/*.h`, tolerable only under D8's ABI freeze — so any `kernel-shared` ABI change requires re-running `build-sysroot.sh`

- **Files, end to end — the MFS server, the FS band, and VFS's read path (slice 5.8):** the **FS band is `FS_RQ_BASE = 0x900`**, which was the last reserved slot, so **`0x700..0xC00` is now fully allocated** (PM/VFS/FS/BDEV/CDEV) — a tenth band needs a home outside that span, and `the_server_band_space_below_vm_is_fully_allocated` replaces the test that recorded `0x900` as free. The request set is **`FS_READSUPER` + `FS_LOOKUP` + `FS_READ` and nothing else**: no PUTNODE (MFS keeps **no per-open state** — there is no node to put, which is also why `VFS_CLOSE` sends the FS nothing), no stat (`FS_LOOKUP`'s reply carries mode + size), no GETDENTS — the `CDEV_READ` precedent that a request without a consumer is better absent than stubbed. **The path travels inline** (`FS_PATH_OFF`, NUL-**padded** to `FS_PATH_MAX = 64`, so the longest path is 63 bytes and a field with no NUL is `ENAMETOOLONG` rather than a truncation that could resolve to another file): it is control plane, not the data path D4 provisioned grants for — the `PM_EXEC` name / `DS_PUBLISH` key precedent — it costs MFS no staging buffer (its scarcest resource), and it deletes the confused-deputy question because there is no granter. Data travels by grant with **no granter field and no grant-offset field** (VFS issues a fresh grant over exactly the round's bytes). **An over-long `FS_READ` is clamped — a short read, not `EINVAL`** — the deliberate departure back towards `CDEV_WRITE`: BDEV refuses because *its* client is a filesystem that cannot interpret half a block, but here the client is VFS, whose job is hiding staging from POSIX, and a read is short at EOF regardless. **Two copies, not one** (device → MFS's block buffer → the caller's granted buffer), unlike the 5.4 write path's advertised single copy: a MinixFS read is rarely block-aligned at both ends and a *hole* has no device block to copy from at all — MINIX 3's own shape. **`fs/mfs` is split unusually hard because `[[bin]] required-features = ["server"]` removes `main.rs` from every CI job** (clippy `--all-targets`, miri, llvm-cov — none passes the feature): every line with a decision in it is in the lib (`proto.rs` wire codec, `walk.rs` traversal + read policy, the `Vec`-free rewrite of `mkfs-mfs`'s `verify.rs`), mitigated further by one extra `cargo clippy -p minixrs-mfs --features server` step in `ci.yml` and a note in `Cargo.toml`; `kernel/build.rs` threads `--features server` through the nested build the way it threads PM's `--no-default-features`. `proto.rs` re-derives its own `rd_i32`/`rd_u64` because `server-rt` is an *optional* dep — the trade `userland/init` already makes. **The 4 KiB block buffer is a `.bss` static, not a `main`-frame local**: a server stack is exactly one page, so a local would put the frame base *below* the mapping and the fault becomes a VM SIGSEGV that prints nothing `qemu-boot.forbidden` catches. This does **not** contradict TTY's "stage in `main`'s frame, not a static" — that rule's load-bearing half is *the buffer outlives every call that names it*, and a static satisfies it strictly better (the address never changes, so MFS's grant to MEM is issued once at boot and `ensure_registered` never re-fires). It is reached only through the **`Blocks` capability token**, whose `read(&mut self) -> Result<&[u8; N], i32>` makes "hold a directory block across the next fetch" a **borrow-check error**; `uspace::SERVER_STACK_BYTES` exists solely to carry `fs/mfs`'s `const _` tripwire for that, and `userland.rs` const-asserts its own stack mapping against it. **Two error-relay rules that read as contradictory and are not:** a `BDEV_READ` failure becomes **`EIO`** (MFS's client addressed a *file*), while a `SYS_SAFECOPY` failure against VFS's grant is relayed **verbatim** (`EPERM` vs `EFAULT` are different caller bugs — the 5.3 rule). MFS is **degraded, never fatal and never a panic** past `sef_startup` (a failed mount ⇒ `ENODEV` to everything, MEM's `blocks = 0` precedent), and **every device-derived loop bound has a cap** (`walk::dir_size`'s `MAX_DIR_BYTES`, `size < 0 → EIO`, `zone_ok` before every read) — a corrupt `size = i32::MAX` would otherwise spin MFS, blocking VFS, blocking init; VFS's probes cannot reach that class, which is why it needs unit tests. **VFS side:** `VFS_OPEN 0x801` / `VFS_READ 0x802` / `VFS_CLOSE 0x803` (`NR_VFS_MSGS` 1→4); `VFS_READ` **reuses `VFS_WRITE`'s payload verbatim**, which is why `write.rs` is now `rw.rs` (`advance`'s four rules are direction-agnostic — "a peer reporting 0" *is* EOF) with a new `open.rs` for what differs. **VFS reads the path with `sys_copy(caller_e, …)`** — the first live consumer of D4's `SYS_COPY`-for-control-plane sentence, and the confused-deputy rule in its sharpest form: `SYS_COPY` has **no per-target authorization at all**, so a payload-supplied source would let any client read any process through VFS. **VFS does not loop on read** (POSIX allows a short `read()`; it loops on `write` because it may not). `fd.rs` gains `Fd::File { ino, pos }` with **no cached size** (EOF is `n == 0`, one source of truth, and a cached size is what 5.10's writes would invalidate), `NR_FDS` 4→8 (so "lowest free" and "table full" are distinct tests), and interior-mutable `UnsafeCell<[FdRow; N]>` storage — **whose rule is never hold a table borrow across a SENDREC**; `Fd` is `Copy` so the borrow dies at the destructuring `let`. `alloc_in` scans **upwards** from fd 3: a `.rposition()` returns 7 and passes every "did I get a descriptor" check. `do_write` gains `Ok(Fd::File { .. }) => EROFS`, defined and refused rather than folded into the unused case — the `BDEV_WRITE` precedent and 5.10's one-line landing site. **VFS's `bdev_demo`/`bdev_denials` retired**: MFS is the real BDEV client, so the ten-probe battery relocated to `[diag mfs]` verbatim and VFS lost its `rootfs::*`/`BDEV_*`/`GET_RAMDISK` imports. **DS ordering is a chain now** — `ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs`, satisfied only by array position in `kernel/build.rs`; both new lookups have `boot_endpoint` fallbacks with distinguishable diag lines, and `bdev.ds ok` / `fs.ds ok` are what pin them. **`kernel-shared::rootfs` gained the image's *contents*** (`ROOTFS_MOTD`, `ROOTFS_PATTERN_*`, `ROOTFS_HELLO_PATH`, `rootfs_pattern_byte`) so `build_rootfs` lost its literals and MFS's read proof is a *check* rather than a transcription. **The landmine slice 5.8 had to defuse:** init's `("no-such", VFS_WRITE + 1, …, ENOSYS)` probe became `VFS_OPEN` the moment the band grew — a real request answering `EINVAL`, silently retiring `vfs.deny ok n=4` while every other marker stayed green. Band-relative (`VFS_RQ_BASE + NR_VFS_MSGS as i32`) is the only spelling that survives a growing band; write every unknown-request probe that way

  things at once (slice 5.9, D6; Phase 5 complete):** `SYS_EXEC` gained a **source selector**

  covers "a boot-archive module" and "the file VFS staged". `4..20` stays `argv[0]` *and* the proc
  name in **both** forms; only where the bytes come from changes. The loader reads through
  `boot_image::elf::ElfSource` — an **enum, not a `dyn` trait** (no vtable per header field) with

  `copy_from_user_as`, so there is **no new copy machinery**; the per-page segment copy stays a
  single copy in both forms. The grant is validated by `do_safecopy::verify_grant` (widened to
  `pub(super)`), *not* a second copy of its eleven checks, and the read completes **before the point
  of no return**, so a granted buffer that is not an ELF leaves the target on its old image.
  `load_exec_image` takes an `ElfSource` and returns `Result<_, i32>`, ending the fold-everything-
  into-`ENOMEM` stance: `Map(OutOfMemory)` → `ENOMEM`, `Source` → `EFAULT`, else **`ENOEXEC`** — and

  **`kernel/build.rs`'s pack-time `scan_brand` cannot reach a file**, so the runtime scan is the
  only gate: `brand::scan_note_segment` is split out (pure, host-tested; `scan_brand` delegates) and
  the loader stages each `PT_NOTE` through a bounded stack buffer — a brand past `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` is
  not found, impossible for anything this repo's `user.ld` rule produces. `p_memsz`/`e_phnum` are
  now *input* rather than build output, so `kernel-shared::execimage` carries `MAX_PHNUM`,
  a **cumulative** `PageBudget` (per-segment checking misses a hundred reasonable-looking segments),
  and `segment_end`; all pure and host-tested, the standing rule for predicates `kernel/src/` cannot
  test. **The boot-archive `hello` module is dropped** — keeping it would leave the five C markers
  unable to distinguish a boot-archive exec from an FS one (the 5.5/5.6 byte-identical-markers
  trap), so `name=hello src=grant entry=` deliberately keeps `name=` and `src=` **adjacent**: one
  substring proving program *and* form. `worker` stays boot-embedded as the name-form regression.
  **A leading `/` is `PM_EXEC`'s only discriminator** (one field, because two can disagree; and it
  is already the FS band's rule), which also settles `com::ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME`'s warning — module
  names and paths are disjoint namespaces, so nothing resolving a *path* can name the `rootfs` blob.
  **`argv[0]` is the path's basename, never the path**: that single choice left `EXEC_NAME_LEN`,
  `PROC_NAME_LEN`, `execstack::INITIAL_STACK_MAX`, `worker`'s `ARGV0_NAMES` set, and the

  **`server-rt::rd_name` cannot express a NUL-padded field's rules**: it reports "no NUL anywhere"
  and "a full-width name" identically, and those are `ENAMETOOLONG` and `EINVAL` — so PM's
  `path::parse` takes the payload's whole fixed-width field as **raw bytes**. Caught by a boot
  probe, not by review; apply it to every fixed-width inline field. VFS's 256 KiB staging buffer is
  a `.bss` static for MFS's `BlockBuf` reason (a one-page server stack), but needs **no capability
  token and no borrow discipline** — VFS never dereferences the staged bytes, so the buffer's
  address is all it wants and the crate keeps zero `unsafe` blocks. Nothing releases the stage

  exec. **`VFS_EXEC_STAGE` carries the path inline** (its client is PM, which already holds it
  inline — no `SYS_COPY`, and no source process to misname) and **a short stream is `EIO`, not a
  short stage**: an ELF cannot be loaded in pieces by a loader with no filesystem, the one place in
  VFS where a partial transfer is not a legitimate answer. **The fd-table debt `fd.rs:48-60`

- **The MinixFS write path — allocation, splicing, and the write-back condition (slice 5.10a):**
  `FS_WRITE = FS_RQ_BASE + 3` (`NR_FS_MSGS` 3→4) **reuses `FS_READ`'s payload field for field** —
  inode, grant id, byte count, position — because it is the same question in the other direction,
  so one wire codec and one clamp serve both; only the grant's direction bit differs (`CPF_READ`
  here, `CPF_WRITE` there, checked by the kernel's `verify_grant` and re-implemented by no server).
  **A short `FS_WRITE` is normal, and that is not an inconsistency with `BDEV_READ`'s
  refuse-or-nothing:** BDEV refuses because *its* client is a filesystem that cannot interpret a
  fraction of a block, while this request's client is VFS, whose whole job is hiding staging from
  POSIX — the same reasoning that made `CDEV_WRITE` short-write and `FS_READ` clamp. There is still
  **no granter field and no grant-offset field**, so **VFS re-grants per round** (a fresh magic
  grant over exactly the bytes that round will move, revoked after), where the CDEV loop instead
  advances a payload `offset` against one standing grant. Do not add an offset field to buy the
  other shape: re-granting is what keeps the confused-deputy surface at zero and costs one kernel
  call a round.
- **What the single block buffer forces (5.10a, continued).** MFS has exactly one 4 KiB `.bss`
  block buffer (slice 5.8's `Blocks` capability), and that constraint — not taste — fixes
  `do_write`'s step order: read the inode, clamp, compute the grown size, *place the zone*, then
  read-modify-write the data block, then write the inode back. Nothing may hold a block across the
  next fetch, so every intermediate is a `Copy` scalar and `place_zone` must finish with the buffer
  free. `Blocks` gained `buf_mut` and `write` for this, and its standing grant to the `memory`
  driver widened to **`CPF_READ | CPF_WRITE`** — one buffer, both directions, one static address,
  so `ensure_registered` still never re-fires. Widening the flags does **not** widen what any one
  call may do (the kernel checks the direction per call), but it *does* re-arm anything that used
  `blocks.gid` as a deliberately-insufficient grant: MFS's `bdev.deny` battery had a probe doing
  exactly that, and it needed its own `CPF_WRITE`-only grant aimed at block 1 (the block
  `START_BLOCK = 2` leaves spare) in the same change, or the probe would have written MFS's block
  buffer over the superblock.
- **Two ordering rules in the allocator — the first mutation-proved, the second UNPROVEN
  (5.10a, continued).** A zone's **bitmap bit is set before its number is stored**, so a mid-write
  failure leaks a zone rather than letting two files share one — the recoverable failure over the
  corrupting one. That one is mutation-proved. The second is not, and the difference matters. The
  inode write-back is keyed on **"a zone was assigned *or* the size grew"**, never on the size
  alone: filling a hole in the middle of an existing file assigns `zone[i]` without moving `size`
  at all, and keying on size would drop that pointer while leaving its bitmap bit set — the bitmap
  and the inode disagreeing about a live zone, corruption rather than a leak. **Know that the
  second half of that condition has no boot probe**: init writes strictly sequentially, so every
  assignment also grows the size, and dropping `dirty` from the condition moved *no* marker under
  mutation. It is a correct invariant guarding a case nothing can reach until there is an `lseek`
  or a truncate — treat it as unproven, not as covered, and probe it in the slice that adds one.
- **`/etc/scratch` and the marker that has to fail two ways (5.10a, continued).** `mkfs-mfs` ships
  `/etc/scratch` **empty**, so every zone the file ends up with — the indirect block included — was
  allocated at runtime; init writes `ROOTFS_SCRATCH_LEN` = 32 KiB to it (eight blocks: seven direct
  zones plus one indirect, crossing the seam at 28672, the `/etc/pattern` reasoning one layer up),
  closes, **re-opens** (a fresh `FS_LOOKUP`, so a size that never reached the inode is a short read
  rather than something a descriptor remembered — nothing on this path caches a size), and compares
  **every byte**. `minix.rs init: fs.write ok n=32768 v=32768`: `n=` is what the write path
  reported, `v=` what read back correct, and they fail independently. Verify the **whole file**, not
  windows — there is no `lseek`, so reaching any offset already read every byte before it, and the
  three-window version this slice started with left offsets 4096..28671 read but never compared; a
  mutation corrupting one byte in the second direct zone printed `ok` under the windows and
  `fs.write FAIL verify off=4096` under the full compare. Both numbers are literals (init cannot
  format an integer), pinned to the constant by a `const _`.
- **The 5.8 lesson, second occurrence (5.10a, continued).** `open_denials`' `write-file` probe
  asserted `EROFS` from `write()` on a file descriptor — and the moment the write path became real
  that probe stopped being a denial and became a **successful overwrite of `/etc/motd`**, silently,
  with every other marker still green. Retired, and `open.deny ok n=8` → `n=7` so the retirement is
  a visible diff rather than a deletion nobody reviews. Same shape as 5.8's `VFS_WRITE + 1` probe
  becoming a real `VFS_OPEN`. **Write every denial probe so that a growing capability makes it fail
  loudly, not pass vacuously** — spell unknown-request probes band-relative, and never aim a
  "must be refused" probe at a file or block whose accidental write would destroy something.

- **`FS_CREATE`/`FS_TRUNC` and the flags field `VFS_OPEN` gained (slice 5.10b):**
  `FS_CREATE = FS_RQ_BASE + 4`, `FS_TRUNC = FS_RQ_BASE + 5` (`NR_FS_MSGS` 4→6). `FS_CREATE`
  **reuses `FS_LOOKUP`'s wire codec verbatim, request and reply alike** — same question, with the
  file brought into existence first — so it still has no granter field and no grant-offset field.
  `VFS_OPEN` gained `VFS_FLAGS_OFF` (an i32, `fcntl`'s values) without moving `NR_VFS_MSGS`: a new
  *field* on an existing request, not a new request. `O_CREAT` on a lookup miss dispatches to
  `FS_CREATE`; `O_TRUNC` on a lookup hit dispatches to `FS_TRUNC`; `O_CREAT | O_TRUNC` on a miss
  takes the create arm and stops, because a fresh file is already empty — so the truncate, when it
  runs at all, runs before the descriptor is installed, and a failure never leaves a descriptor
  onto a half-truncated file.
- **The staging-buffer invariant, and why it is not a rollback (5.10b, continued).** `do_write`'s
  create path now copies the client's bytes into a second 4 KiB `.bss` buffer *before anything is
  allocated*, so no client-controlled failure can occur after an allocation. Clearing the bitmap
  bit on that error path would have been actively *wrong* for an indirect slot whose indirect block
  already existed on disk — the block still names the zone, so freeing the bit hands one zone to
  two files, corruption rather than the leak. This is the fix for the reachable denial of service
  5.10a named and deferred.
- **`find_free_slot` must let `Occupied` beat `Free` across *every* block of a directory, not just
  within one (5.10b, continued).** Scanning block-by-block and returning the first free slot found
  is backwards: a name that already exists in a later block gets shadowed by a duplicate insert
  into an earlier block's free slot — silently, no error, no marker. The fix scans every block for
  the name first and only then reuses a free slot.
- **Two orderings this slice cannot prove, named rather than omitted (5.10b, continued).** The
  mutation matrix confirmed both are unreachable by anything this system can induce: reversing
  `do_trunc`'s free-before-write-back order moves no marker, and inserting the dirent before
  `write_inode` in `create` moves no marker either — both need a failure *between* two steps that
  nothing here can trigger. This is the 5.10a `dirty`-condition lesson applied to two new rules
  rather than repeated by omission. Contrast `bitmap_clear`'s off-by-one, which also moves no boot
  marker but *is* caught by two host tests in `fs/mfs/src/write.rs` — a real proof, just not at the
  boot-log layer.
- **`/full` and `/etc/holey` exist because two arms are otherwise unreachable in *both* boot
  configurations (5.10b, continued).** `/` holds 5 entries and `/etc` 7, against 64 slots per
  block, so without a directory that is exactly full no create would ever grow a directory; and
  with no `lseek`, init writes strictly forward, so only a pre-existing hole below EOF reaches the
  "zone assigned but size unchanged" half of 5.10a's write-back condition. `/etc/holey` is what
  finally proves that invariant.
- **A denial probe's flag must be spelled relative to `O_KNOWN`, not as a literal (5.10b,
  continued).** `fcntl::O_UNKNOWN_BIT` is *derived* from `O_KNOWN`, so a flag becoming real makes
  the probe fail loudly instead of passing vacuously — the same lesson as spelling unknown-request
  probes band-relative.
- **The boot budget moved a third time: 240 s → 600 s (5.10b, continued).** Measured the same way
  as before — the last required marker's byte position as a fraction of a fixed-timeout log, on
  the musl flavour, against the merge base: 26.90% → 61.61%, a 2.29× jump, leaving a 1.62× safety
  factor at the old budget (below the 1.78× that forced the previous raise). The 256-probe leak
  battery (each a doomed grant plus a BDEV round trip) is the dominant cost. One methodology note
  worth keeping: `MINIXRS_SDK` does **not** persist across separate shell invocations, so a
  measurement that sets it in one command and boots in another silently measures the SDK flavour —
  check the embedded `hello` size (~200 KB musl, ~47 KB SDK, ~15 KB fallback) rather than trusting
  the build warning.
- Also worth a line: the image went to **128 inodes**, `mkfs-mfs` learned **sparse files**
  (`Manifest::add_sparse`), and `kernel/build.rs` now asserts free-inode headroom against the
  **built** image beside the existing free-zone assert.

- **`/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, and `CDEV_READ` (slice 5.11):** `CDEV_READ = CDEV_RQ_BASE + 1`
  (`NR_CDEV_MSGS` 1 → 2) is `CDEV_WRITE`'s payload with the copy reversed — the grant carries
  `CPF_WRITE`, the driver pushes with `SAFECOPY_TO`, **`0` is EOF and a short read is legal**, so
  VFS sends one request and never loops (the `FS_READ` stance). The 5.3 plan text saying 5.11
  would be "minors, not requests" was wrong for *reading* zero; four in-tree copies of it were
  corrected. `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` are **CDEV minors 3 and 5 of the memory driver**
  (MINIX 3's `NULL_DEV`/`ZERO_DEV`), and **minors are a per-driver namespace**: the same driver's
  ramdisk is BDEV minor 0, the request band tells them apart, and nothing asserts `CDEV_MINOR_*`
  against `BDEV_MINOR_*`. The memory driver **never clamps** — `CDEV_MAX_IO` protects TTY's
  stack staging buffer and there is no staging here — so a null/zero write answers the whole
  count with **no copy at all** (an unmapped buffer *succeeds*, Linux's behaviour: never aim a
  `bad-buf` probe at `/dev/null`), and a zero read fills the whole request from a 256-byte
  static in `CDEV_MAX_IO` steps, reporting partial progress on a mid-way failure (5.4's rule).
  The four-field CDEV parse lives in **`server-rt::cdev`** now that two drivers decode it;
  validation stays per driver. VFS's `Fd::CharDev { dev: CharDriver, minor }` names its driver
  (an enum, not an `Endpoint`, because `DEFAULT_ROW` is a `const`), and `servers/vfs/src/dev.rs`
  is a three-row **device-node table** consulted **after the path copy and before the mount**
  (a device open needs no filesystem; `O_CREAT`/`O_TRUNC` ignored on a hit; exact byte match, no
  `/dev` on the image, `/dev/other` falls through to MFS's `ENOENT`). **A console `read()` is
  now a real `CDEV_READ` to TTY**, which answers `ENOSYS` from its unknown-request arm until
  Phase 6 — same errno init's `read-console` probe always expected, now the driver's answer
  rather than VFS's guess, so Phase 6 adds one TTY arm and touches VFS not at all. The memory
  driver's validator is probed from VFS's prologue (`mem.deny ok n=5`, last, after `fs.deny`),
  including the first `CPF_WRITE`-required refusal on the CDEV band (MFS's `bdev.deny` battery
  already exercises the same kernel check on a `BDEV_READ`). init's
  `dev.console ok` is written **through** the `/dev/console` descriptor, never fd 1: that is the
  only thing that proves the table row points at TTY. Paths are `callnr::DEV_*_PATH` so init and
  VFS cannot drift.

## Documentation

Canonical docs are an **mdBook in `book/`** (content under `book/src/`, TOC in
`book/src/SUMMARY.md`), published to GitHub Pages on push to `main` via
`.github/workflows/docs.yml` (path-filtered to `book/**`; mdBook pinned to 0.5.3; Pages
actions SHA-pinned like `ci.yml`). Write new documentation there, derived from source —
the `docs/*.md` files are legacy bootstrap notes being retired. The planning tree is the
exception and stays: `docs/plan.md` is the lean live tracker (phase status + slice
summaries), and `docs/plans/` holds the full per-phase slice histories
(`phase-2-ipc.md` / `phase-3-vm.md` / `phase-4-servers.md`), the pre-Phase-5 cleanup
tracker (`phase-5-prep.md` — one PR-sized chunk per session, same markers), and the
Phase 5 design + slice plan (`phase-5-musl-fs.md` — locked decisions D1–D13 and slices
5.0–5.11 with per-slice scope/proof; read it before starting any Phase 5 slice). Build
locally with `mdbook build book`; output `book/book/` is gitignored.

To install mdBook or preview the book locally, use the `mdbook-preview` skill.

**Slices are built with the superpowers skills as of 5.10a** — `brainstorming` for the design,
`writing-plans` for the task breakdown, `subagent-driven-development` to execute it (a fresh
subagent per task, a review after each, then a whole-branch review). The per-slice design and
plan documents land in **`docs/superpowers/specs/`** and **`docs/superpowers/plans/`**, named
`YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-{design,plan}.md`. That is a third documentation tree and it is deliberately
narrow: `book/` stays canonical for how the system works, `docs/plan.md` + `docs/plans/` stay
canonical for slice *status*, and the superpowers tree holds the reasoning behind one slice —
the decisions considered and rejected, the per-task steps, the verification plan. The phase
tracker links to the spec by relative path rather than restating it; keep it that way, or the
two drift and the tracker is the one people read.

Two habits from 5.10a worth keeping, both of which caught real defects that slice-level review
missed. **Give a fresh reviewer the diff as a file** and ask it to verify arithmetic by hand
rather than confirming that tests exist — that is what caught a tautological cap test whose
assertion held with the clause deleted. And **run the whole-branch review against `book/`**:
every task in a subagent run sees one crate, so nobody re-reads the published docs, and 5.10a
reached its final gate with the mdBook still asserting `BDEV_WRITE` answers `EROFS`. `docs.yml`
is path-filtered to `book/**`, so a slice that forgets the book ships a Pages site contradicting
its own code, silently and indefinitely.

A third habit, from 5.10b, and the sharpest one: **the dominant defect class in a subagent-driven
slice is a doc comment or test that was true when written and was falsified by a LATER TASK IN THE
SAME BRANCH.** Five instances in one slice — a `Blocks::zeroed` comment saying mkfs writes no
sparse files (task 2 added them), a `next_dir_chunk` comment saying its second iteration is
unreachable at boot (task 8's probe reaches it), two copies of an indirect-slot count that was
simply miscomputed, and worst, `callnr.rs`'s `vfs_open_payload_offsets_are_ordered_and_disjoint`
— whose `assert_eq!(fields.len(), 2, "a VFS_OPEN payload field was added")` and accompanying
"there is no `flags` field until 5.10b" comment were left untouched **by the task that added the
flags field**, disarming the very tripwire written to catch it. Each task sees one crate and no
task re-reads its neighbours' prose, so nobody catches these. Make it a whole-branch step: grep
the touched crates for every `unreachable`, `nothing reaches this`, `there is no X yet`, and
`until slice N` claim, and for every `assert_eq!(fields.len(), N)` or similar count-the-fields
tripwire, and check each against what the branch actually added. **A tripwire the adding branch
does not grow is worse than none**, because it reads as coverage.

That sweep is owed by a **review-fix round** too, not just by the slice, and a rename or a
moved path is its loudest trigger: a reviewer works finding-by-finding inside one crate, so
the copies living in `book/`, `tests/qemu-boot.expected` and `docs/plans/` are exactly the
ones nobody looks at. 5.10b's review named three falsified claims; grepping the old names
across the whole tree found four more (`book/`'s `insert_entry`, two `/etc/deny` comments in
VFS, and the expected-marker file's commentary on a probe that had been re-aimed). Run
`grep -rn '<old name>' --include='*.rs' --include='*.md' .` before committing, every time
something is renamed or relocated.

A review fix that **rewords a claim** owes the same sweep as a rename: 5.11 corrected
"the first `CPF_WRITE`-required refusal" in four files and left the fifth copy in
`tests/qemu-boot.expected`'s commentary. Grep the *phrase* across `tests/ book/ docs/
CLAUDE.md` before committing any review fix. And read every `book/` chapter a slice
touches **end to end once**, not diff-wise: 5.11's two remaining defects were
self-contradictions 190 and 24 lines apart in the same chapter.

`docs/plan.md` and the `docs/plans/*` files track slice/chunk status with three markers: `◀ next` (unstarted), `◀ ready (branch ..., pending merge)` (implemented but unmerged), `✓ shipped (PR #N, merged YYYY-MM-DD)` (merged). Flip the previous slice forward and slide `◀ next` ahead as part of each slice's PR — in **both** plan.md's summary line and the corresponding `docs/plans/` detail file. When opening a new slice PR, also reconcile any older `◀ ready` markers against `git log` — stale "pending merge" labels on already-merged PRs accumulate otherwise.

Mutation tests (the 5.1/5.2/5.3 standard: apply, observe the named marker move, revert) run against an **uncommitted** working tree, so never revert one with `git checkout <file>` — copy the files to the scratchpad first and restore from there, then `diff -q` each back and `grep -rn MUTATION` to prove nothing leaked into the PR. A mutation that fails to **compile** is indistinguishable from one that worked: `kernel/build.rs` panics on the nested server build, the log holds no kernel output at all, and `check-boot-log.sh` reports every marker MISSING. Before recording any observation, `grep -a 'error\[E' <log>` or confirm unrelated markers still PASS (slice 5.4 nearly recorded a false result this way). Iterate and mutation-test in the **stub-free** config: 5.10b measured the `fs.*` markers at ~0.14% of a 60 s `--no-default-features` log, so `timeout 30` sufficed for nine boots that would each have cost 240 s otherwise — judge such a run by grepping the specific marker, since `check-boot-log.sh` FAILs the stub A-D markers there by design. Not every mutation moves its predicted marker, either: reordering the MXBI packing does **not** reliably break a DS lookup, because publish-before-retrieve is scheduler-dependent and often still resolves — to exercise a DS *fallback* branch, remove the peer entirely or break the key (slice 5.7 got that observation from the drop-the-server mutation instead, and slice 5.8 reconfirmed both halves: the `memory`/`mfs` swap moved nothing, while breaking MFS's `"memory"` DS key gave `bdev.ds FAIL rc=-3 fallback=3`). Some correct invariants have **no** mutation that moves anything, and the honest record says so rather than omitting the row: 5.10b found two orderings (truncate's free-after-write-back, create's dirent-after-`write_inode`) whose violation needs a failure *between* two steps, where the only available failure is `EIO` from a fixed RAM ramdisk whose block numbers are bounds-checked before they leave MFS — no probe can induce one. A third, `bitmap_clear` off by one, moved no marker either but **is** caught by host unit tests, which is a different situation worth distinguishing: before recording a row as uncovered, run `cargo test` under the mutation too, not just a boot. A guard's mutation moves the marker of the **probe that exists for that guard**, not a marker on a healthy path — a healthy path never trips it. Slice 5.8's plan predicted that deleting MFS's `!node.is_dir()` guard would break `fs.selfcheck`; resolving `/etc/motd` only ever walks real directories, so what actually moved was `fs.deny FAIL not-dir`. Relatedly, never copy a **count** into a marker from a plan — recompute it from the constant (5.8's plan said `n=30` for a 31-byte `ROOTFS_MOTD`). The scratchpad snapshot must cover the files a slice **adds**, not just the ones it edits: `git checkout -- <untracked file>` does not restore, it *errors* — and behind a `|| true` it leaves the mutation in the tree (slice 5.9 did exactly this to a new `servers/pm/src/path.rs`). Snapshot every file you will mutate before the first run, and let the final `grep -rn MUTATION` sweep — never the restore command's exit status — be what proves the tree clean. Two mechanics from 5.11: rust-analyzer diagnostics (`dead_code`, unused imports) that appear mid-run are usually residue of a mutated or half-edited file — trust `cargo clippy … -D warnings` on the committed tree, not the IDE. And the boot-ratio's `git checkout --detach <merge-base>` needs a clean tree: commit the marker edits *first*, detach, boot, then check out the branch again. Stage by explicit path — `git add $(git diff --name-only)` sweeps in a locally modified `.claude/settings.json`.

## Review tooling: Hunk

Code review happens in a live Hunk diff session in the user's terminal, driven from
here with `hunk session …` (never `hunk diff`/`hunk show` directly — the TUI is the user's; the
`hunk-review` skill at `hunk skill path hunk-review` has the full CLI). Two standing rules:

- **Open every session with `--experimental`** (`hunk diff --experimental origin/main...HEAD`), so notes can
  carry STML. A session without `stml` in `hunk session context --json`'s `experimentalFeatures` rejects
  markup and silently falls back to plain summaries.
- **Author notes in STML, not plain text** — `hunk session comment apply … --stdin` with a `markup` field per
  item, `--summary` kept as a real one-line fallback. Read `hunk markup guide` first and preview at the
  session's `noteMarkupWidth` with `hunk markup render - --width N`. `<code>` is a *block* tag: identifiers
  inline go in `<c fg="accent">…</c>`; `↔` is not an entity, use the literal `↔`. A useful shape is a
  severity `<badge>` + bold title, a rounded `why` box, a rounded `fix` box, and a dim `see also` line.
- PR review comments (Grok, a reviewer) get mirrored into the session as one `comment apply` batch, one
  note per thread anchored at the thread's `newLine`, `author` set to the reviewer's name.
